text: Presenting to the broader engineering team is a different job than briefing leadership. This room already understands Kubernetes scheduling and cluster-wide averages — they need the honest mechanism and a clear ask, not a concept re-explained.
Theo runs the meeting close to the Lesson 15 report's own order: timeline, root cause, the fix shown next to its validation data, explicit credit for what went right, then the follow-up actions.

What keeps this blameless is how the meeting is run, not just the report's wording. Theo keeps the conversation on the missing constraint and the dashboard's design gap, redirecting anything that drifts toward whose fault it was.

The follow-up table doesn't stay a table. Each action becomes a tracked ticket live in the room, owner confirmed out loud, due date open to pushback. This closes out the incident, and the capstone moves on to what leadership asks next.
